name: Connla Cóel
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: More than a dozen Irish figures share the name Connla. One Connla was the son of the hero Colsen. His mother was the warrior woman Ayin. He met his father in Ulster and refused to give his name. He fought his father and was killed by him. A second Connla, called Connla Colo, is a king of the fairies. A third, Connla of the Golden Hair, is the son of the king of Tara. He left the earth with a woman of the fairy race to win endless life.
